Here is a concrete, highly recommended 5-day itinerary for your trip to Paris, starting on **June 10, 2026**. 

Because June is one of the most beautiful (and popular) times to visit Paris, it is highly recommended to book major entry tickets (especially for the Louvre, Versailles, and the Eiffel Tower) several months in advance.

---

### **Day 1: Arrival & Iconic Landmark Views (Wednesday, June 10, 2026)**
*   **Morning/Afternoon:** Arrive in Paris and check into your hotel. Take some time to unpack and freshen up. Start your trip with a leisurely stroll along the **Seine River** to shake off any jet lag.
*   **Late Afternoon:** Head to the **Trocadéro Gardens** for the absolute best view of the **Eiffel Tower**. Walk down across the Pont d'Iéna to stand directly beneath this architectural marvel. 
*   **Evening:** Embark on an evening **Seine River Cruise**. Seeing the historic monuments of Paris light up from the water as the sun sets is the perfect way to welcome yourself to the City of Light. Follow this with a casual dinner at a nearby bistro.

### **Day 2: Historic Heart & World-Class Art (Thursday, June 11, 2026)**
*   **Morning:** Beat the crowds at the **Louvre Museum** (reserve the earliest timed-entry slot). Focus on major highlights like the *Mona Lisa*, *Venus de Milo*, and the *Winged Victory of Samothrace*, or wander through the stunning French Sculpture wing.
*   **Afternoon:** Exit through the glass pyramid and stroll through the manicured **Tuileries Garden**. Grab a legendary hot chocolate or pastry at *Angelina* on Rue de Rivoli. Walk past the **Place de la Concorde** and take a scenic stroll up the famous **Champs-Élysées** to the **Arc de Triomphe** (climb to the top for spectacular radial views of Paris's avenues).
*   **Evening:** Spend your evening in the lively **Latin Quarter**. Wander its narrow, medieval winding streets and enjoy a traditional French dinner at a cozy local spot.

### **Day 3: Bohemian Montmartre & Île de la Cité (Friday, June 12, 2026)**
*   **Morning:** Spend your morning in **Montmartre**, the historic hilltop artist enclave. Walk up the winding cobblestone streets to the steps of the breathtaking **Sacre-Cœur Basilica** for a sweeping panoramic view of the entire city. Stop by the **Place du Tertre** to see local painters at work.
*   **Afternoon:** Head down to the historic island in the center of Paris, **Île de la Cité**. Marvel at the restored exterior of the **Notre-Dame Cathedral**, then step inside the nearby **Sainte-Chapelle** to experience its breathtaking, floor-to-ceiling 13th-century stained glass windows.
*   **Evening:** Explore the trendy **Canal Saint-Martin** area, popular with locals. Enjoy a relaxed dinner of modern French cuisine or share small plates at a trendy wine bar along the canal.

### **Day 4: Day Trip to the Palace of Versailles (Saturday, June 13, 2026)**
*   **Morning & Afternoon:** Take a short 30-minute ride on the RER C train from central Paris to the magnificent **Palace of Versailles**. 
    *   *Inside:* Explore the breathtaking **Hall of Mirrors**, the King’s Grand Apartments, and royal bedrooms. 
    *   *Outside:* Spend hours wandering through the endless, meticulously manicured **Versailles Gardens**, designed by André Le Nôtre. June is the perfect time to catch the famous Musical Fountains Show.
*   **Evening:** Head back to Paris. Treat yourself to dinner in **Le Marais**, one of Paris's most historic, vibrant, and fashionable districts, filled with incredible architecture and dining options.

### **Day 5: Impressionist Masterpieces & A Grand Farewell (Sunday, June 14, 2026)**
*   **Morning:** Visit the spectacular **Musée d'Orsay**, housed in a stunning Beaux-Arts railway station. It holds the world’s largest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces, featuring works by Monet, Van Gogh, Renoir, and Degas.
*   **Afternoon:** Spend your final afternoon enjoying the relaxed Parisian lifestyle. Rent a green metal chair in the gorgeous **Luxembourg Gardens**, read a book, watch the model sailboats on the pond, and enjoy a final scoop of famous *Berthillon* ice cream.
*   **Evening:** Celebrate your final night with an unforgettable farewell dinner at a classic, grand Parisian Brasserie—such as the historic **Le Train Bleu** (inside Gare de Lyon) or the beautiful Art Nouveau **Bouillon Julien**—for a classic meal of steak frites and profiteroles.
